pr_body:
This is a new node, intended as a replacement for the current `ParallaxBackground` and `ParallaxLayer` workflow. In contrast to `ParallaxBackground`, `Parallax2D` inherits from `Node2D`, which provides a few benefits over the old workflow:

- Automatic adhering to the current camera's transforms (rotation, zoom, etc)
- Able to be modified and transformed with non-parallax textures
- Compatibility with `CanvasGroup`
- More performant
- Flexibility to be used in or outside a `CanvasLayer`
- Ability to override the number of repeats for zooming out or rotating the camera
- Auto-scroll feature

The inspiration for this was a few pain points regarding the old workflow. There's still a lot to work on, as I'd like some community feedback and to add some more (reasonable) helpful features, but this is a good start with feature parity to the old system. I have a few ideas to fix some more issues, like handling zoom-out repeats, and some editor guides, but this is a nice beginning.

This should close quite a few old open issues:
Fixes: #22453, fixes: #30988, fixes: #39347, fixes: #42586, fixes: #67120, fixes: #77827
Possibly fixes: #63352, #71701, #82380, #87317

Also implements the following proposal:
Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8779,
Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8107,
Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7237

Obviously, this is too much of a breaking change to flat out remove the old workflow, but with this the `ParallaxBackground` and `ParallaxLayer` nodes can be deprecated for removal in a later version. In the meantime, I was able to retrofit the new changes for mirroring into `ParallaxBackground`, so users who aren't ready for a change can still benefit from a speed up. Here is my cursory benchmarks:

2500-2600 FPS: `ParallaxBackground` with 8 `ParallaxLayer`s while scrolling (master branch)
4100-4200 FPS: `ParallaxBackground` with 8 `ParallaxLayer`s while scrolling (Parallax2D branch)
4400-4500 FPS: 8 `Parallax2D`s while scrolling
4900-5000 FPS: Empty scene

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/e1bbbda2-35c1-40f5-b685-c3081101dc53

Here it is working in a `CanvasGroup`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/bce7a70b-80f2-40fa-99b7-b0624fe67539

Also thanks to our neighborhood svg wizard @MewPurPur for the quick work on an alternative icon!

Any and all feedback is welcome!
pr_comments:
I just started with a feature to add number of repeats. This is to address the issue some users face when zooming out on an infinite repeat background since it only draws twice per.

The performance isn't bad. Even with 8 layers with 5 repeats (36 copies per item per layer), it still performs better than `ParallaxBackground` on master, but obviously it's not free or infinite. You'd still need to update it when you're zooming out, but this at least provides an avenue for those who need it. That being said, you could also just set your texture to repeat and make it large enough for the size of your screen zoomed out. Either way, there should be a note about performance when doing this with a large number of large textures.

Before:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/51e980c2-f3fd-4754-8352-80a4b3aabe6d

After:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/9fac15d5-b14a-4854-8a40-ac4db84928bf

Also added a highly requested `autoscroll` feature, since it doesn't affect much and was easy enough to implement. I think that's all I want to start with, so I'm gonna open this up for review. I think it'd be great to have some editor guides, but I think we should have a discussion on what that should look like, since parallax is hard to visualize, and too much going on may cause more confusion than help.

The most common request I've received on this PR is to allow updating its position while in the editor. Until now, I had a warning that would show when the position was moved in the editor. Since overriding the position is how this node works, I was having trouble thinking of solutions that would satisfy this request, but I think the best way forward is to update the `scroll_offset` to whatever the `position` is while in the editor. That way, running the game, what you see in the editor will match what's on screen.

This leaves one question unanswered: Should updating the scroll update the local position or the global position?
Global position would be more of a "it just works", but less flexible. Local position would be more flexible and accurate, but is easier for users to get an undesirable result.

Thoughts?

I was thinking about one last more last minute addition, if anyone thinks this would be a big help. A drawback of parallax backgrounds is that if you're doing an infinite repeat, there's no way to have more than one per scene. Any extra ones would overlap the ones behind it because there's no beginning or ending (it's infinite). To help with this, in addition to `limit_begin` and `limit_end`, I've added `clip_begin` and `clip_end` properties. These lets you clip anything outside the specified boundaries, so you can have two different areas that lead into one another:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/61db176e-94a2-4775-9da2-d2d9769670af

I can't think of any workaround for this, so this may be very helpful. Anyone have any thoughts?

I thought of a workaround, but it seems there's problems with both solutions.
The workaround is to put the parallax layers in a `Node2D`, put that in a `Control` and set it to `clip_contents`, then offset the `Node2D` back to `0,0`. It's a little hacky, but I was actually calling the same method `Control` uses, so this may be more ideal since you can surround multiple `Parallax2D` nodes at once.

Unfortunately, it looks like the rendering server has a bug that makes all clipping ignore camera rotation, so it loses some of the benefits given by `Parallax2D`, but that confirms that there isn't an ideal solution without further bug fixes to the renderer. I'm going to not add the properties to avoid too much bloat, since neither the work around or the built in properties avoids the renderer bug.

It looks like it increases the size to fit the rotated items, but still ignores the camera rotation:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/21325943/fc1a8143-8129-4ce4-aa90-7ac35195789e)
I may want to hold off having this feature. This new Parallax2D node is really good as is, in all honesty (Refer talking to other developers in RocketChat. It's easier that way).

If this is merged for 4.3, I would rather deprecate before the release the older parallax nodes. Especially if the user have to choose between non-compatible nodes.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/270928/9e771998-adf2-4028-83f1-66c3838edc75)

I gave it a test in my project. Overall it seems similar to my custom system (the old one, not the one I showed in the proposal), in that you can get reliable results in an intuitive way. It also has the same problems with fitting the background within room confines ([example of wrongly fit background](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/ac49ca43-bad9-49f8-ab0f-dba4e9329877)). However I think there is no reasonable way to prevent that, other than using some "layer anchors" or whatever.

The good news is that by using `screen_offset` it's easy to preview the background in the editor, which makes it even more convenient to work with.

EDIT:
I'm wondering about `override` properties. Things like screen offset or viewport following should be set to the same value for every Parallax2D node. As it is now, if you don't use defaults, you need to remember to set them for each node, which is inconvenient. Not sure how to solve it (other than adding a new ParallaxGroup2D node, which is probably overkill).

EDIT2:
The `follow_viewport` property is magical to me. On my first try, the parallax was broken, because I was using a CanvasLayer. So I enabled `follow_viewport` in CanvasLayer and it was fixed. Then I tried the `follow_viewport` in Parallax2D; when it's disabled both in CanvasLayer and parallax, the background scrolls as expected. I just don't get it, but cool that it works xd

> I'm wondering about `override` properties. Things like screen offset or viewport following should be set to the same value for every Parallax2D node. As it is now, if you don't use defaults, you need to remember to set them for each node

In a lot of case multi-selecting nodes (Holding CTRL/Shift and selecting in the Scene tree) can easily circumvent this. Perhaps something in the documentation should also hint towards the properties in override needing to be consistent between parts of the same background.

I totally forgot you can multi-select them and edit them all together. That makes this super easy. Thanks for the tip!

Regarding KoBeWi's second edit, I'm just gonna post this here again for reference:
`follow_viewport` kind of replicates the behavior of `ParallaxBackground`. Weirdly, `ParallaxBackground` is a `CanvasLayer` with `follow_viewport` disabled by default, but is still following the viewport with custom logic, so it's kind of misleading. That's why with `Parallax2D`, I have `follow_viewport` enabled by default because it does in fact cause it to follow the viewport unlike `ParallaxBackground`. Disabling it while in `CanvasLayer` would be the obvious choice, because `CanvasLayers` don't move with the viewport either unless overridden. Of course, if you want to have the parallax be a child of a `CanvasLayer` that has `follow_viewport` enabled (which overrides it's default behavior and makes it behave like it's not a `CanvasLayer` but a normal node), then you can leave the `Parallax2D`'s `follow_viewport` at its default (enabled).

So I decided to take a step back and actually try replicating the same results using the current ParallaxBackground workflow.
For the record, my main problem with the old workflow is that the stuff you place in ParallaxLayer ends up in completely different positions once you start your project. This was however resolved by #58567, but since I already had my workflow, I did no go back to ParallaxLayers to test it.

So what I did now was start with the background I had setup with the new Parallax2D, replace my scene root with ParallaxBackground and all Parallax2D with ParallaxLayers, then copied `scroll_scale` to `motion_scale` and `repeat_size` to `mirroring`. Doing just that I got the same result as with Parallax2D, so the new workflow is not that different.

There are caveats:
- there is no autoscroll. I didn't expect it to be built-in though, as it can be easily solved with a script
- mirroring is limited to 1 repeat. Having more can be convenient for smaller textures

I also tried to replicate my editor preview and with ParallaxBackground it doesn't seem possible. `scroll_offset` that should be used for this has no effect in the editor (I didn't check the source for why). Enabling it would probably allow for easy editor preview.

As it stands now, for my purposes the relevant stuff from the new Parallax2D is increased repeat and the ability to preview it in editor. But that's me; since it brings more than that, it's still worth considering.

Thanks for testing it out! I'm glad you were able to to replicate your setup without complications. If you encounter any problems, please let me know!

I know that for your needs you may not see much difference, but the main benefits I was trying to provide that `ParallaxBackground` does not:

1. Rotates and zooms with the current camera.
2. Ability to be modified and transformed with non-parallax textures
3. Compatibility with `CanvasGroup` (!!!)
4. Flexibility to be used in or outside a `CanvasLayer`
5. More performant
6. Overcome the zoom-out limitation of `ParallaxBackground` with `repeat_times`

Auto-scroll feature isn't a must, but was highly requested by most of the users I had try it out. The argument was that it's a pretty commonly used QoL, there's no performance cost if you don't use it, and very little if you do, so why not?

If it were possible to just modify `ParallaxBackground` I would, but the fact that it inherits from `CanvasLayer` is its biggest flaw. The other thought I had was to just modify `ParallaxLayer`, but it's too many changes to force on a user in between major versions, so a new node is the only option forward.

I now noticed your solution for `scroll_offset`. There is an easier way to do that - by overriding `_edit_set_position()`. GraphElement has an example of that.
Also if the `position` is irrelevant, you can disable it using `_validate_property()` (I assume it shouldn't be saved to scene either).

Seems like `scroll_scale` moving does not work well with `screen_offset`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/40da36a8-65ea-4031-ad0c-db22529659a4

It's bad, but adjusting `screen_offset` and then moving the node is not really a common operation, so it's fine if you won't fix it.

@KoBeWi Interesting, and great call out! It looks like it has to do with your `limit_begin` and `limit_end` values. Maybe I should make that only be taken into consideration outside of the editor.

EDIT: Yep, wrapping the limit part of the scroll update in an editor check fixed the editor issue.

I wouldn't be against it, but I was looking through the code base, and though there are dozens of nodes flagged as experimental, `GraphEdit` is the only one with a configuration warning. Is there a reason for a warning for `GraphEdit` and no others?

GraphEdit had a warning because we already knew we were going to change its implementation, so using it was especially risky. The warning now should maybe be removed if it's still there, I think the API is mostly finalized? CC @Geometror 

So here just experimental without warning seems good to me, it communicates that we _may_ change things but it's not a big risk that needs to be flagged explicitly via an always-on warning.
Will give this a final deeper review as soon as I'm able, hopefully tomorrow

Trying it out in 4.3dev5, works great from my initial testing. My main gripe is that it uses top left of the screen instead of the center, I think there should be a toggle to use the screen center, and maybe let you input a custom center value (should have both, as the former would go towards the center no matter the resolution). Also not sure if this is in scope of the node, but maybe a sort of "perspective mode" could be nice to have? Basically, multiply the offset by the scroll scale. So with lower scroll scale, the object slowly goes towards the center, which can create a "building from above" effect. For this the toggle above could be important as it would let you input a custom center point. This is relatively easy to make yourself (so I left some code below), but it could be nice to have as a built-in feature.
Example and Code
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/98223724/4226528c-1137-44cb-b9aa-9623d615d51e) ![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/98223724/0de1f88d-270a-48cb-8c85-c2a55f681fb9) ![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/98223724/f469d72d-1764-47b7-8c89-0be12d9b25ea) ```py extends Node2D @export var scroll_scale: Vector2 = Vector2.ONE @export var scroll_offset: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO @onready var original_position: Vector2 = global_position @onready var camera: Camera2D = get_viewport().get_camera_2d() func _process(delta): global_position.x = lerp(camera.get_screen_center_position().x + scroll_offset.x, original_position.x, scroll_scale.x) global_position.x = lerp(camera.get_screen_center_position().y + scroll_offset.y, original_position.y, scroll_scale.y) ```
Also I found documentation bug, `Less than 1 scrolls slower, making object appear *closer*` should be "further".

@ettiSurreal I appreciate the feedback! This initial PR is mainly focused on being able to replicate the behavior of `ParallaxBackground` but in a friendlier format. It's awesome to see others interested in improving the usability and features of the new node and it's designed specifically to be built on top of. I'd encourage you to open a proposal for some of your ideas and how to implement them, so it can get some more visibility and interest!

For this the toggle above could be important as it would let you input a custom center point. This is relatively easy to make yourself (so I left some code below), but it could be nice to have as a built-in feature.

I also want to add to this and ask if we can have an option to scale objects according to perspective scale as well? So we can have objects appear smaller as their distance is further away. 

And on top of that, an equivalent to "Preview Canvas Scale" but for this instead, since we can't really preview the parallax effect in editor like we could with ParallaxBackground. This is mainly so we can preview the background as a pseudo-3D space. I'm not sure how much work that is, but it'd be nice to have, and is one big feature I feel is missing in this one.

> I know https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8779#issuecomment-1902164761 that supports editor perspective before I even started work on this PR

btw I managed to recreate more or less the same thing using Parallax2D (it's easy using `screen_offset`, the tricky part is setting up the preview area to look like in-game), but I also want to figure out how to make it editable while previewing.

It's probably too late. But this guy made a [plugin](https://github.com/nklbdev/godot-4-previewing-parallax-background) to preview parallax in the editor. I don't know if it can be replicated in the new system.

That'd be up to the developer of that plugin to adjust to, if it's even needed, but that wouldn't really change the decision or progress of this PR, you should probably talk to them about this instead

> While I'm here, though, I've heard the technique you mentioned once or twice, but I haven't found any official documentation on this (just a few random comments from users on forums).

I think this is the only "official" mention: https://godotengine.org/article/godot-32-will-get-pseudo-3d-support-2d-engine/
God damn genius! This will be awesome!

Hey, just because it was asked, and I'm current working with Parallax in my project. It was a huge problem for me working with parallax and split screen. Reason being, because parallax inherits from canvas layer, it makes its contents to be dependant on the viewport.
The old implementation from my understanding requires the content of the canvas layer to be _duplicated_ for each view. If there's any element that should be synchronize, that can easily turn into a nightmare. So my solution for now was to not use parallax layers at all, instead, using an intricate setup of viewports and cameras. It is cumbersome, but does the job, so I only have to worry about background objects in one place.
Since the new system is moving away from canvas layers to node2d, I assume it's possible that the problem doesn't exist anymore. Each new parallax layer is displaced according to the camera position as expected, I hope. If split screens are a factor to be considered at all, I find to be worth testing this.

@FrederickKDP Thanks for the interest! This PR is closed, so it'd be best to open a discussion regarding this. Feel free to tag me, since I'm currently looking at good ways to accomplish split screen easily! In the meantime, please take a look at this proposal to make this easier. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10014

issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.1-stable

**OS/device including version:**
Issue found in:

Linux 5.0.0-32-generic #34~18.04.2-Ubuntu SMP Thu Oct 10 10:36:02 UTC 2019 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
00:02.0 VGA compatible controller: Intel Corporation HD Graphics 620 (rev 02)

macOS Catalina 10.15.4
AMD Radeon Pro 5300M 4 GB

(Issue found too with nvidia card)

**Issue description:**

We found an issue using particles2D:
We created into our project a Particles2D which has a process material (shader) programmed by scratch. The affected sprite which is failing is placed into a parallax layer, which is also placed into a parallax background having layer = -100. 
The issue makes the background sprite to dissapear.
Also, the Particles2D is placed on the main player's layer. After the issue occurs, if we hide the Particles 2D, the background sprite appears again, and also dissappear if we enable it again.
While there are other particles in the screen emmited by other particles2D, the sprite also appears.

Finally, we detected something relevant: in case we set the background parallax layer to a positive value or 0, the background appears and some other sprites dissappears from the screen.

We attach a video with the issue and the shader code.

**Steps to reproduce:**

Create a scene with a Particles2D with a Shader as a Process Material, but we are not sure 100%.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[Issue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4740868/Issue.zip)
